title: SO-F-08 Admission adapter boundary: the admission service behind an adapter beside the merge boundary, trust consumed only as an eligibility input of the admission path, external admission before the node's own, degraded mode reported, and both services named generically
request: Build layer of the Scope One programme, adapted from the unsigned fold of 30 Oct 2026 (fold id SO-F-08) and validated against memev main at d1c65ef. Contracts marked with a dagger are signed in the owner's vault and are not visible in this repository; they are cited by id only. Implements the design record SO-2.13 (Commercial integration services that keep the open-core boundary neutral) (contracts/scope-one/specs). The decision record cites this contract by id and keeps only the gaps this one does not cover. Builds on signed vault contracts: WO-05-A†, WO-05-D†. Memev contracts that land first: SO-F-03. Page: docs/FEDERATION.md comes from the federation architecture documentation (PR #223, branch docs/federation-architecture, not on main); until that merges, the first contract to need a page creates it with its Status section, labelled planned or architectural target, and the later ones extend it. Source in the fold: #222 section 13.7 (accountable admission; trust governance does not replace access control or evidence) and #223 ARCHITECTURAL-INTERDEPENDENCIES.md (trust governance must not take over semantic correctness); WO-05-D (the trust service specification). Settled decisions this contract follows (owner decision 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md): topology is local-first and the cloud is only a relay and a backup; every supported provider stands on equal footing and no work or tier depends on one; crdt-merge is reached only through the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs (docs/EXTENSION-POINTS.md) and this contract adds no merge engine to the core; tiers follow docs/PRICING.md (Free core, Personal for up to 3 computers with no per-computer add-on, higher tiers by contacting us) with no Personal trial; the git backup keeps running every few minutes (sync.interval_min). Memory authority: ADR 7 (memory and project-state authority) is proposed in PR #325 and is not decided here; this contract cites it and the local-first decision, and keeps one store under the vault with no second database. Provenance: adapted from the unsigned fold of 30 Oct 2026. Changes: (1) converted from the vault task format to the memev spec format (named tests run as red-green checks on the own test file of the contract; inline regular expression flags became the flags key; hygiene and decision verifiers became commands or doc checks). (2) removed fold-only fields and the owner-decision marker field, reworded the stop rule that named a patent, and made the text pass the leak scan. (3) Decision verifier D-SO-E4 replaced by a leak-scan criterion and a doc grep: the generic naming is enforced by the existing scan. (4) AC05 (the two product names added as hashes) dropped: it cannot be built from the repository without holding the names. The owner action is one line in scripts/leak-denylist.json, noted in the log; the file leaves scope. (5) Duplicate removed: the trust adapter is the boundary of PG-09.1 WP09-02 (docs/EXTENSION-POINTS.md, src/engine/acfa-boundary.mjs). This contract owns the admission adapter and the rule that the admission path reads trust only as an eligibility input.

tasks.description: The documents name an accountable-admission service and a trust-governance service as complementary infrastructure. WO-05-D specifies the trust service on the engine's side of the external boundary (docs/PAID-TRUST.md); neither may be credited with guarantees beyond its contract. This contract places both behind adapters shaped like the merge boundary, with inputs, outputs, guarantees, timeouts and degraded mode stated in docs/EXTENSION-POINTS.md; the admission path of src/engine/federation reads trust as an eligibility input only, never as access control or proof; external admission precedes the node's own admission (SO-F-03) when configured. Both services stay generically named (D-SO-E4), and the leak scan enforces that.

criteria.statement: the admission adapter states its inputs, outputs, guarantees, timeouts and degraded mode in code and in docs/EXTENSION-POINTS.md beside the merge boundary; a stub implementation exists for the tests, and the stub trust adapter implements only the interface of PG-09.1 WP09-02 (the trust boundary is owned there, referenced and not redefined); a missing adapter leaves the free behaviour unchanged

stop_rules: Stop and post BLOCKED when a criterion cannot pass without weakening a test, skipping a test or relaxing an assertion.
Stop and ask when the work would name a client product, a person, a server or a seat in repository text; the client names live in docs/CLIENTS.md only.
Stop when the work would add a runtime dependency, a model call, a network call at install or start, a second store for project state, or any reporting that is not opt-in and off by default.
Stop when the work would move convergence logic into the core, vendor the engine, or add a merge engine beside the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs.

Stop when the work would implement a federation, replication, trust, admission or computation feature beyond the specification, schema, validator and conformance test the contract names; the product keeps the planned label on it.
If any criterion fails after the fix: STOP, report the measured result, the failing check and file:line. Do not start the next task.
If the work needs a path outside scope: STOP and ask the owner to amend the contract. Never widen scope silently.
